summary: Heng Sure is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Oakland University, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union under Ronald Y. Nakasone and Hsuan Hua. He has held professorships at the Graduate Theological Union, Bond University, and Dharma Realm Buddhist University.

Henk Blezer works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his doctoraal studies at Leiden University, where he also served as a postdoctoral researcher (1993–1997) and teacher of Buddhist studies (2002–2008), alongside a post at the International Institute for Asian Studies (1997–2001).

Henk Bodewitz was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. He served as assistant professor (1966) and chair of Sanskrit (1976–1992) at Utrecht University, and as associate professor (1976) and professor (1992–2002) at Leiden University.

Henri Bergson was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Condorcet, École Normale Supérieure, and the University of Paris. His career included teaching at the Lycée David d'Angers (~1881–1883) and holding a post at the Collège de France (1900–1904).

Henri Cordier worked in sinology, history, and archaeology after studying at Lycée Chaptal. He served as a professor at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales from ~1881 to 1925 and at Sciences Po from ~1886 to 1925.

Henri Gaidoz worked in linguistics and related fields. Educated at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Albrecht Weber (1865), he taught geography and ethnography at Sciences Po (1872–1908) and served as directeur d'études for Celtic philology at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from 1876.

Henri Hubert specialized in religious studies, history, and archaeology. Educated at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and École Normale Supérieure, he held posts at the National Archaeological Museum (~1898–1927), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1901–1927), and École du Louvre.

Henri Maspero was a scholar of sinology, linguistics, and religious studies who studied under Édouard Chavannes. His posts included the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, the Collège de France chair of sinology (1918–1945), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1919–1944).

Henri Massé worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Algiers from ~1916 to 1927 and at the École des langues orientales from ~1927 to 1958.

Henri Pirenne was a historian who studied at the universities of Liège, Frederick William Berlin, Leipzig, and Paris, as well as EPHE. He held posts at the University of Liège (~1885–1886) and Ghent University, serving as professor of history (1886–1931).

Henrik Samuel Nyberg worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies. Educated at Uppsala University (from 1908), he taught at Fjellstedt School (~1916–1919) and served as docent and professor of Semitic studies at Uppsala University (~1919–1956).

Henry Beveridge was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Glasgow (~1853–1857) and Queen's University Belfast (1856). He served in the Indian Civil Service (1857–1893) and was president of The Asiatic Society (1890–1891).

Henry Clarke Warren specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Harvard University, Johns Hopkins University, and the University of Oxford, receiving instruction from Charles Rockwell Lanman (1879), Maurice Bloomfield (~1881–1884), and T. W. Rhys Davids.

Henry George Keene worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Fort William College and Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge, later serving with the East India Company (~1798–1811) and as professor at East India Company College (1824–1834).

Henry Hamilton Hadley worked in religious studies and linguistics, studying at Yale and Andover Theological Seminary. He taught sacred literature (1858) and Hebrew (1862) at Union Theological Seminary and held a professorship of Hebrew at Yale Divinity School (1861).

Henry Herbert Dodwell was a historian and Indologist educated at Lord Williams's School and St John's College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Education Service (1908–1922) and was professor of history and culture at SOAS University of London (1922–1946).

Henry M. Hoenigswald was a linguist who studied at the universities of Munich, Zurich, Padua, and Florence between 1932 and 1936. He spent the major part of his career on the faculty at the University of Pennsylvania (~1948–1985).

Henry Martyn was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. He received his education at Truro Cathedral School and St John's College (~1797–1801), and he studied under John Borthwick Gilchrist from ~1804 to 1805.
Henry Miers Elliot was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Winchester College (~1821–1826) and served as a civil servant for the East India Company from ~1826 to 1853.

Henry Pitts Forster was an Indologist and linguist. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (~1783–1815) with the East India Company and was Master of the Calcutta Mint at the India Government Mint, Kolkata, in 1803.
